div.div:
أَشَلُّ A man whose hand, or arm, has become unsound, or vitiated: (S, TA:) or deprived of the power of motion by an unsound, or a vitiated, state of its عُرُوق [meaning veins or nerves]: (Msb:) or dried up, or stiff: or whose hand, or arm, has gone [or wasted] away: (K, TA:) fem. شَلَّآءُ. (S, Msb.) ―
-b2- And يَدٌ شَلَّآءُ (Mgh, TA) A hand, or an arm, that will not comply with that which its possessor desires of it, by reason of disease therein. (TA.) ―
-b3- And عَيْنٌ شَلَّآءُ An eye of which the sight has gone. (O, Msb, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
